title: TLS Certificate Validation
source_note: Inspired by Apple's famous 'goto fail' TLS bug.
summary: Review this certificate-validation helper and find the single line that fatally changes the control flow.
explanation: The unconditional 'goto fail;' exits the verification path even when hashing succeeded, so the later signature verification never meaningfully protects the handshake.
hints: The flaw is in the verification flow, not the setup code.
One line exits early even when the previous operation succeeded.
Look for a control-flow statement that skips the final cryptographic check.
The unconditional jump on line 31 is the problem.

title: Community Vault Withdrawal
source_note: Inspired by The DAO reentrancy bug family.
summary: This withdrawal flow mostly reads cleanly. Find the one line that creates a dangerous interaction order.
code: event Withdrawal(address indexed account, uint256 amount);
explanation: The contract sends value to the caller before updating their stored balance. A malicious receiver can re-enter withdraw while the old balance is still intact.
hints: The bug depends on the order of side effects.
State is updated too late relative to an external interaction.
Find the line that hands control to attacker-controlled code before the balance changes.
The external call on line 22 should not happen before the balance update.

title: Guidance Packet Builder
source_note: Inspired by the Ariane 5 numeric-overflow failure pattern.
summary: This telemetry encoder narrows floating-point measurements into a compact packet. Find the conversion that can catastrophically break on large values.
code: private static short checksum(short[] packet, int length) {
explanation: Casting an arbitrary scaled double straight to short can overflow or truncate catastrophically when the measured value exceeds the destination range.
hints: The flaw is not in the loop or checksum logic.
Look for a lossy conversion that assumes the input always fits.
One line narrows a larger numeric representation without a bounds check.
The cast on line 27 can overflow the packet field.

explanation: Line 4 indexes into the collection with a parsed external value before checking whether it falls inside the valid range. An out-of-range input will panic.
hints: The parse step is not enough by itself.
The flaw is not about the element type but about when validation occurs.
Look for the first direct use of the parsed index.
The unchecked index access on line 4 is the bug.
